analyst_view.overall: Early view: a Breton derby at Roazhon Park, four days before Rennes host Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League. Rennes' games have been the most open in the league (42 goals in 10), and Brest are in good form under Julien Lachuer, with both sides in the league's top four for shots per game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, already high. I stay with it: Rennes score and concede about two a game, and Brest score 1.8, so goals are likely at both ends. Esteban Lepaul's fitness (ankle) and Brest's centre-back injuries are the things to check nearer the time.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, with 6.5 for Rennes. I lean slightly lower: Rennes average 5.7, and Brest's direct, low-possession play produces few corners (one against Lyon). Nine or ten rather than eleven.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: it is a derby, and Brest are 4th in the league for fouls (14.2 a game). Derby intensity plus Brest's physical approach makes five or more bookings plausible.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots. I lean higher: Rennes average 16.2 shots a game (3rd) and Brest 16.1 (4th), which sums to over 32. Even allowing for a tighter derby, the high 20s look likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean higher: Rennes are 2nd (6.0 a game) and Brest 3rd (5.7) for shots on target. Both goalkeepers should be busy.
